blocks.md: This lesson follows **Trustworthy Operational Logs** in *Supervisory Intervention* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Supervisory Intervention, § Trustworthy Operational Logs
blocks.md: Consider a robotic arm striking a warehouse racking upright during a supervisory takeover. If the operational log contains an unrecorded gap, investigators cannot determine whether the policy proposed the damaging trajectory, the enforcer admitted it, or the operator received authority too late to intervene. Rigorous incident reconstruction requires two foundational properties: declared loss handling and an operational record engineered to survive physical failure.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Authority record matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: The authority record binds a sealed static authority manifest to a per-tick evidence tuple of time, authority state, measured state, proposed and admitted commands, so every handover is reconstructable and attributable.

questions.q: The section **Trustworthy Operational Logs** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Per channel, authority resolves every tick to exactly one state with the enforcer the sole actuator writer, and a four-phase request-acknowledge-commit-release handshake moves it.

The authority record binds a sealed static authority manifest to a per-tick evidence tuple of time, authority state, measured state, proposed and admitted commands, so every handover is reconstructable and attributable.

Supervisory intervention transfers the right to propose on named actuator channels from the policy to an authenticated person, committed on a control tick and bounded by a lease, while every human command still passes the permission check.
Single-writer gating resolves arbitration faults but not mode confusion, the gap between the mode a supervisor believes and the actual one, which only per-channel masks and annunciation fix.
